chief_complaint: recurrent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain relieved by hot showers
hpi_details: A 77-year-old male with long-term frequent cannabis use presents with recurrent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain relieved by hot showers. The episodes have gradually worsened.
ideas: He thinks he caught a stubborn stomach bug or developed a food sensitivity that only settles down when he stands under hot water.
concerns: He is worried that losing so much weight and being unable to keep food down will force him to give up living independently.
expectations: He hopes to receive IV fluids and a strong anti-nausea medication so he can stop vomiting and return home today.
social_hx: Non-smoker, social drinker, long-term frequent cannabis use

investigation_events.title: Point-of-care dehydration and electrolyte results
investigation_events.availability_message: The point-of-care dehydration and electrolyte results are now available; antiemetic care and rehydration should not be delayed.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome (CHS) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome (CHS) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes counseling on complete cessation of cannabis and using capsaicin cream for acute relief, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: recurrent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain relieved by hot showers
Key HPI features: A 77-year-old male with long-term frequent cannabis use presents with recurrent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain relieved by hot showers. The episodes have gradually worsened.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome (CHS).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Cyclical vomiting syndrome without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

Ignoring critical warning signs such as: persistent vomiting despite hot showers and cannabis cessation, signs of dehydration or acute kidney injury from prolonged vomiting, or new presentation at advanced age without a long personal history of heavy cannabis use.
management_principles: Counsel on complete cessation of cannabis, capsaicin cream for acute relief
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of recurrent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain relieved by hot showers. HPI: heavy chronic cannabis use.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome.
reference_soap.plan: Counsel on complete cessation of cannabis as the only definitive treatment, and offer topical capsaicin cream for acute symptom relief. Ensure hydration and correct any electrolyte abnormalities from prolonged vomiting. Consult gastroenterology if symptoms persist despite cannabis cessation.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome
Implement evidence-based management plan: Counsel on complete cessation of cannabis, capsaicin cream for acute relief

teaching.one_liner: Heavy, long-term cannabis use paradoxically triggers cyclical bouts of severe nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain that are classically relieved by hot showers or baths.
red_flags: Persistent vomiting despite hot showers and cannabis cessation — atypical for CHS and warrants workup for another cause (e.g., bowel obstruction, pancreatitis)
Signs of dehydration or acute kidney injury from prolonged vomiting
New presentation at advanced age without a long personal history of heavy cannabis use — raises suspicion for an alternate diagnosis (malignancy, gastroparesis) rather than CHS

must_ask.say: How much cannabis do you use, and how often, and for how long have you been using it?
Do hot showers or baths seem to ease the nausea?
Do these episodes come in cycles, with periods where you feel completely fine in between?
How severe is the vomiting, and do you have abdominal pain with it?
Have you lost any weight because of these episodes?
Do you use any other recreational drugs or drink alcohol?

history.answer: Doctor, I have been having terrible bouts of nausea and non-stop vomiting, along with an aching pain in my belly.
These episodes started happening every few weeks over the past few months, but this current flare started two days ago and has been getting steadily worse.
During these attacks I vomit five or six times a day, occurring both after I try to eat and on an empty stomach.
It is mostly clear to yellowish fluid and stomach bile, with no bright red blood or dark coffee-ground material.
The nausea is definitely worst first thing in the morning when I wake up, but the vomiting is not projectile or shooting across the room.
It is a dull, crampy ache all over my abdomen, and throwing up does not relieve the pain at all.
The belly pain is around a five out of ten, but the nausea is unbearable, easily a ten out of ten.
I am still passing gas and had a normal soft bowel movement yesterday, with no diarrhea, constipation, or severe bloating.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
My wife ate the exact same food as me and feels completely fine, and I haven't eaten anything spoiled.
I haven't had any headaches, neck stiffness, blurred vision, or confusion, just lightheadedness when I stand up.
No, I haven't hit my head or had any falls or injuries recently.
I can barely keep sips of water down, my mouth is parched, and I've noticed my urine is quite dark and very little comes out.
No excessive urination or unusual thirst before this illness began, and I do not have diabetes.
No chest pain, chest tightness, palpitations, or shortness of breath.
I have lost about six pounds over the past month because I lose my appetite during these episodes.
No, I definitely never make myself throw up on purpose; it just comes on uncontrollably.
I have been smoking cannabis almost daily for more than twenty years to relax.
The only thing that brings me relief from the nausea and stomach pain is taking long, scalding hot showers or hot baths.
Yes, it happens in cycles where I feel sick for a couple of days, then feel mostly fine for a few weeks before it hits again.
I do not use any other recreational drugs like cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, or painkillers.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like high blood pressure, diabetes, or kidney disease.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I don't take any regular prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or other substances.
No, I have never smoked tobacco or cigarettes.
I drink alcohol only socially, maybe one beer or a glass of wine once or twice a month.
I am a retired teacher and live at home with my wife.
There is no family history of stomach cancer, ulcers, gallbladder disease, or bowel disorders.
I thought I might have picked up some kind of recurring stomach bug or food allergy, since standing under a hot shower is the only thing that calms my gut down.
I'm really worried that if I keep losing weight and throwing up like this, my family will think I can't live on my own anymore.
I'm just hoping you can give me some IV fluids and a strong medicine to settle my stomach so I can head back home.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 114/72 mmHg, pulse 92 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Lying blood pressure 114/72 mmHg with heart rate 92 beats/min; on standing, blood pressure drops to 104/64 mmHg with heart rate rising to 108 beats/min.
Oral mucous membranes are dry with sticky saliva; pharynx is clear without redness or exudate.
Decreased skin turgor with slight skin tenting; capillary refill time is approximately two seconds.
Abdomen is flat and symmetric without surgical scars, visible peristalsis, or distension.
Normoactive bowel sounds heard across all four quadrants without bruits.
Mild diffuse tenderness on deep palpation throughout the abdomen; abdomen is soft with no voluntary guarding or rigidity.
No rebound tenderness elicited in any quadrant.
Alert, attentive, and fully oriented to person, place, and time.
Supple neck with normal passive flexion; Kernig and Brudzinski signs are negative.
Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light; extraocular movements intact without nystagmus.
